name: Infectious Epithelial Keratitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Infectious Epithelial Keratitis

criteria.description: Presence of corneal epithelial defect with underlying stromal involvement
Identification of causative infectious agent by culture, PCR, or smear
Characteristic clinical signs including dendritic or geographic ulcers
Improvement of symptoms and signs with appropriate antimicrobial treatment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of corneal epithelial defect with characteristic clinical features plus identification of infectious agent or clinical response to antimicrobial therapy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by microbiological confirmation when possible.

pathognomonic.notes: Classic branching ulceration pattern seen on fluorescein staining
Visible epithelial loss on slit-lamp examination
searchTerms: scratch or defect on eye surface

common.notes: Moderate to severe eye discomfort and light sensitivity
Redness of the conjunctiva surrounding the cornea
Blurred vision due to corneal involvement

occasional.notes: Swelling of corneal stroma adjacent to epithelial defect
Feeling of something in the eye
Presence of cells or flare in anterior chamber

rare.notes: Full-thickness corneal defect leading to globe rupture
Elevated intraocular pressure due to inflammation
Severe intraocular infection as a complication

laboratory: Positive corneal scraping culture or PCR for infectious agents (e.g., herpes simplex virus, bacteria, fungi)
Fluorescein staining showing dendritic or geographic ulcers
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing epithelial defects and stromal involvement
other: Response to antiviral or antimicrobial therapy supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant stromal inflammation rather than epithelial ulceration
Presence of stromal haze and edema without epithelial defect
Rapidly progressive stromal infiltrate with purulent discharge
Usually associated with contact lens use or trauma
Diffuse conjunctival injection with follicular reaction
Subepithelial infiltrates rather than dendritic ulcers

redFlags: Rapidly worsening ocular pain and vision loss
Signs of intraocular infection or endophthalmitis
references: Kaufman HE. Herpes Simplex Virus Keratitis: Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management. Cornea. 2019.
Wilhelmus KR. Diagnosis and Management of Infectious Keratitis. Am J Ophthalmol. 2017.
